content.overview: The final lesson combines safety, biosecurity, controlled instructions, traceability, equipment care, records and handoff into one shift-length Technician I simulation. Learners must identify dependencies before acting, preserve blocked or unresolved work, respond to new conditions mid-case, and leave a reconstructable evidence packet for the next shift.

vocabulary.definition: The collection of current instructions, assignments, records, identifiers, status information and supporting evidence used to complete a task or shift.
Prioritization of conditions so urgent safety, biosecurity, identity, equipment or process risks are addressed before lower-risk production tasks.
A condition that must be resolved or verified before another task can safely or correctly proceed.
Demonstrating multiple competencies together in a realistic workflow rather than answering isolated knowledge questions.

sections.title: Read the whole system before acting
sections.body: Real shifts contain competing priorities and linked controls. A scheduled movement can depend on room status, identity, sanitation, equipment readiness and entry authorization at the same time. The technician first identifies conditions that block downstream work instead of automatically starting the first line on the schedule.

sections.title: Use evidence to choose the next safe action
sections.body: Each decision should be tied to controlled information: current instruction, label/SDS and PPE requirements, entry status, physical identifiers, equipment readiness, traceability event history or factual observations. When evidence conflicts or authority ends, the correct performance is to hold, stop or escalate—not improvise.

sections.title: Finish with a reconstructable shift state
sections.body: The simulation is complete only when records show what was completed, what changed, what could not be completed, which statuses remain active, who was notified, what evidence supports the final physical/record state and what the incoming shift must do next.

workedExamples: A planned plant move is delayed because the destination is held and one identifier mismatches; both controls are preserved and routed before movement.
A sanitation product does not match the controlled instruction, so the learner refuses substitution and uses the contingency/escalation path.
An equipment alarm receives only permitted external checks and a time-ordered maintenance escalation, not an unauthorized repair.
A required historical measurement is missing; the learner uses the missing-data/late-entry process rather than inventing a value.
A work-related symptom pattern is reported factually with task/control context without the technician assigning a medical diagnosis.
The final handoff leads with active restrictions, unresolved identity/equipment conditions and the next time-sensitive event before routine completed work.
commonMistakes: Starting the first assigned task before checking dependencies and restrictions.
Treating documentation as optional because the physical work was completed.
Resolving identity conflicts by relabeling or choosing the most convenient record.
Using more PPE as permission to ignore a restricted area, unclear product or unauthorized task.
Crossing into maintenance because the fault appears simple.
Forcing every task to 'complete' before shift end instead of preserving honest open status.
Handing off vague problems without exact identity, owner, next action or cross-check.
content.practicalApplication: Complete the integrated case in four phases: triage the initial work packet, execute only authorized routine work, respond to new mid-shift conditions, and close the shift with physical/record reconciliation plus a two-way-ready handoff. Produce a complete evidence packet showing every decision and unresolved dependency.
content.summary: Course 1 culminates in integrated operational judgment: work safely, protect biosecurity and identity, follow current controlled instructions, stay within authority, create trustworthy records, reconcile reality with records and transfer unresolved work clearly to the next responsible person.

blocks.title: Capstone rule: do not start with the first line on the task list
blocks.body: Read the entire work packet first. A safety hazard, restricted-entry condition, hold, identity mismatch, sanitation failure or unsafe equipment status can block a downstream task even when that task is first on the schedule.

blocks.title: Phase 1 — triage the shift before work begins

items.title: Review prior handoff and open statuses
items.body: Identify holds, quarantine, restricted entry, out-of-service equipment, open deviations, missing records and time-sensitive next actions.

items.title: Confirm safety / chemical / PPE conditions
items.body: Check hazards, product identity, label/SDS, required PPE and conditions that require stop-work or emergency response.

items.title: Verify controlled instructions
items.body: Confirm current SOP/work orders, scope, prerequisites, acceptance criteria and escalation points.

items.title: Verify identity and destinations
items.body: Match physical identifiers, source/destination, count/quantity and current status before movement/transformation.

items.title: Verify sanitation and biosecurity readiness
items.body: Confirm transition controls, approved products and zone status before introducing people, tools or material.

items.title: Build the dependency map
items.body: Mark every condition that must be cleared or escalated before another scheduled task can proceed.

blocks.title: Initial work-packet triage
rows: Do not move material; preserve hold and route release decision
One source tag does not match movement order
Genealogy may be lost or assigned incorrectly
Stop affected movement and resolve identity before transition
Required biosecurity preparation may not be achievable
Do not substitute; use controlled contingency/escalation
Verify status/authorization and do not treat schedule or PPE as clearance
Crop process may be affected; root cause unknown
Capture fault context, perform permitted checks only and use maintenance path
Historical fact cannot be recreated as contemporaneous data
Preserve missing status and use late-entry/missing-data process

blocks.title: Which issues block the planned plant move?
blocks.setting: At shift start you receive a plant-movement order. The destination room is on hold, one source tag does not match the order, the sanitation station is missing the approved product, and a pump alarm is active elsewhere.
blocks.prompt: What should happen before the move begins?
options: Start moving the correctly tagged plants and resolve the rest later
Clear the destination hold yourself because the movement is scheduled
Resolve or escalate the hold, identity mismatch and sanitation readiness before beginning the movement; handle the pump only within its separate permitted operator process
Ignore the sanitation issue because it is unrelated to identity
blocks.answer: Resolve or escalate the hold, identity mismatch and sanitation readiness before beginning the movement; handle the pump only within its separate permitted operator process.
blocks.feedback: Several controls independently block or condition the movement. Task order does not override hold status, identity control, biosecurity requirements or equipment authority boundaries.

blocks.title: Phase 2 — execute only authorized routine work

items.title: Apply routine controls and verify them
items.body: Correct hazards and readiness issues only when the supplied procedure explicitly gives the technician that action.

items.title: Perform the approved work sequence
items.body: Use current instructions and preserve the required identifiers and traceability events.

items.title: Record observations/events as they occur
items.body: Capture required measurements, movements, checks, exceptions and status changes with enough context to reconstruct them.

items.title: Stop at authority boundaries
items.body: Servicing, release decisions, early-entry/handler authority and other higher-authority actions stay with their controlling roles/processes.

items.title: Keep blocked work visibly open
items.body: Do not manufacture completion simply because the schedule or shift is advancing.

blocks.title: Mid-shift conditions change
blocks.setting: After two routine tasks are completed, a worker reports repeated cough and chest tightness associated with a dusty handling task while the assigned local control is not operating. At the same time, an equipment fault recurs after one permitted reset.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest integrated response?
options: Finish the shift first because neither condition has stopped production completely
Give the worker any available mask and keep resetting the equipment
Use the workplace symptom-reporting/safety process and address the failed exposure control without diagnosing the worker; preserve the recurring fault timeline and escalate after permitted checks
Record both issues as resolved because they were reported
blocks.answer: Use the workplace symptom-reporting/safety process and address the failed exposure control without diagnosing the worker; preserve the recurring fault timeline and escalate after permitted checks.
blocks.feedback: Integrated performance keeps safety, equipment authority and record integrity separate while responding to both changing conditions.

blocks.title: Phase 3 — reconcile physical and recorded reality

items.title: Reconcile identities and locations
items.body: Confirm controlled identifiers and physical locations agree after movement or status changes.

items.title: Reconcile counts/quantities where required
items.body: Compare physical and recorded state without forcing a balance when evidence disagrees.

items.title: Review event relationships
items.body: Confirm new identifiers created by movement/transformation remain linked to source identities and events.

items.title: Close only verified work
items.body: Acceptance criteria and required records must be complete; otherwise preserve open/incomplete status.

items.title: Package deviations and faults
items.body: Make unresolved identity, equipment, sanitation, entry or record issues visible to the receiving role.

left.label: Integrated performance
left.body: Checks dependencies first, follows current instructions, protects identity, works within authority, records facts as they occur, reconciles physical/record status and hands off unresolved conditions.

right.label: Task-completion only
right.body: Focuses on finishing visible physical tasks even when controls conflict, documentation is incomplete, identity is uncertain or the next action exceeds authorization.

blocks.title: Integrated capstone evidence packet
blocks.description: The learner should leave a reconstructable trail showing both completed work and intentionally unresolved work.

fields.label: Priority / dependency map
fields.value: Ranked safety, biosecurity, identity, equipment and production concerns plus blocked downstream tasks

fields.label: Controlled-instruction check
fields.value: Current SOP/work-order verification, scope/prerequisites and conflicts

fields.label: Safety / entry / PPE decision
fields.value: Controlling hazard/product/area-status evidence and permitted response

fields.label: Material identity / traceability decision
fields.value: Proceed, hold or escalate with source/destination/event evidence

fields.label: Equipment fault note
fields.value: Asset, timeline, alarm/symptom, permitted checks, impact, safe status and maintenance escalation

fields.label: Deviation / incomplete-work record
fields.value: Expected state, actual state, sequence, missing information and owner of the open decision

fields.label: Final reconciliation
fields.value: Physical identities, locations, counts/quantities and recorded state comparison

fields.label: Shift handoff
fields.value: Exact open items, notifications, next actions, timing, incoming cross-check and ownership

blocks.note: A capstone answer is not stronger because everything is marked complete. It is stronger when the final records accurately distinguish completed work from work still requiring authorized action.

items.title: Prepare the open-item list
items.body: Prioritize active restrictions, holds, out-of-service assets, discrepancies and incomplete work.

items.title: Exchange task-relevant facts
items.body: Use exact identifiers, observations, status, notifications, next actions and timing.

items.title: Incoming cross-check
items.body: Verify critical status against supplied records, tags, displays or physical condition.

items.title: Read back ownership
items.body: Incoming worker confirms the highest-risk open items and who owns the next action.

blocks.title: Complete the integrated Technician I shift simulation
blocks.instructions: Use the supplied work packet as if starting a real shift. The case introduces new information after the initial plan, so decisions must be updated without losing control of earlier work.
prompts: Create the initial dependency map before performing any task.
Classify each response as routine action, stop/hold, escalation, maintenance referral, safety/health reporting or higher-authority decision.
Show how identity and traceability events are preserved through every permitted movement.
Build a maintenance fault timeline without declaring unsupported root cause.
Document the missed historical measurement without inventing data.
Respond to the work-related symptom pattern without making a medical diagnosis.
Reconcile final physical and recorded state.
Conduct a two-way-ready final handoff with cross-check/read-back of the highest-risk items.
blocks.artifact: Completed integrated work packet with dependency map, controlled-work review, safety/entry decision, traceability record, fault timeline, deviation documentation, reconciliation and verified final handoff

blocks.title: Capstone remediation cue
blocks.body: If the final packet shows every task complete, no uncertainty, no authority boundaries and no unresolved handoff items, inspect it again. Real integrated competence includes recognizing when the correct result is to stop, hold, preserve evidence or transfer a decision rather than force completion.

blocks.title: Course 1 standard
blocks.body: Technician I competence is not knowing every root cause or independently clearing every problem. It is executing routine work safely and consistently, protecting biosecurity and identity, following controlled instructions, creating trustworthy records, recognizing abnormal conditions and escalating correctly instead of improvising beyond role authority.
